pages.head: The Story
pages.html:
TEDDY'S LITTLE BIGGER ADVENTURE

Same little dog. A little bigger adventure.

The Klown Klub's Big Show was a big hit. Doc Leo got his costume back in the nick of time (thanks to a certain corgi), the crowd roared, and the whole Klub paraded through town until midnight with Teddy riding on the roof of THE CHEZ, Doc Leo's little red CitiCar. Gwinn chased the confetti. Everybody went home happy and tired.

Well. Almost everybody.

In the morning, Gwinn's bed is empty. Her pink collar is gone. So is Doc Leo's rubber chicken. A trail of confetti leads out the doggy door.

And Doc Leo has news: the Klown Klub is booked at the Tri-County Fair tonight, way out past the river. The Big Show was big. This show is bigger. Teddy is the opening act.

Teddy will not go anywhere without his big sister. (He will not say so. But he keeps looking at her bed.) So Doc Leo drives THE CHEZ, and Teddy does the sniffing: across town, over the river, through a corn maze and out to the Fair, fetching whatever Gwinn dropped along the way so Doc Leo knows where to drive next.

And where is Gwinn while all this goes on? Every so often the story says MEANWHILE... and then you are Gwinn.

pages.head: Getting Started
pages.html:
Getting Started

Type TEDDY2 and press Enter. You need a VGA display. A Sound Blaster (or compatible) plays the music and the digitized woofs, boofs and sniffs; without one, the PC speaker does its best.

A cartoon plays first (pick Read Storyline to see it again). Press any key for the menu, then pick Play. Leave the menu alone for half a minute and Teddy will show you around Doc Leo's house himself.

There are eight stops. Before each one, a card shows where you are, what to look for, and what is new. At the end of each of Teddy's stops, Doc Leo waits beside THE CHEZ, plugged in at a charger (its charge port is low on the back, on the passenger side). His thought bubble shows what Gwinn dropped there: bring it to him, the car door pops open, and you're off. At the end of Gwinn's stops, hop onto her ride.

Energy and naps

Teddy (and Gwinn) start with 100 energy (the F2 screen calls it Hitpoints) and three naps (Lives). Pests and flying things wear a dog down, and the Fair's bees and popcorn sting the most; bones give 25 back, and they get scarcer the farther from home you go. When energy runs out it's nap time, and you wake at the start of the stop. When the naps are all used up, the game is over.

Press F5 to save your game and F6 to load it.

pages.head: Moving and Hopping
pages.html:
Moving and Hopping

Left Right
or A D		Walk. Gwinn walks faster. Gwinn does everything faster.
Up or WHop! Hold it to hop higher, let go to steer. Gwinn hops higher than Teddy (she is twice his size).
Q EHop up and to the left (Q) or right (E) in one go: the way across stepping stones and over skunks.

Ledges

Awnings, shelves, stairs, branches, the gazebo roof, hay bale steps and the floors of the corn maze can be hopped up through from below and stood on from above. A hole in a floor drops you through; trot fast and you may skim right over a small one.

Things that lift and carry

Doc Leo's bed bounces. The bucket truck's bucket, the mill's grain hoist, the carousel horses and THE BIG DROP ride up and down: step on and hold still. The hay elevator's belt carries Gwinn up to the loft. Rapids carry a swimming dog downstream; the pool and the pig wallow just hold you up.

pages.head: Teddy's Tricks
pages.html:
Teddy's Tricks

Teddy still knows a ton of tricks, and he learned a new one.

SSniff. New! Look for a faint wisp hanging in the air: a scent. Stand by it and sniff, and whatever is hidden there turns up: treats, a bone, a balloon dog, the thing Gwinn dropped, or Gwinn's paw prints pointing the way she went.
SpaceSpeak. WOOF! Dust bunnies, mice, pigeons, ducks and one very groomed poodle clear out.
DownDig. Bones sticking out of the ground, soft dirt with paw prints.
FFetch. Pick up what you're standing on.
1High five. And now: ring the bell. Teddy rings a bell with his paw. Watch where the DING goes: a rung bell drops its ding onto whatever hangs below it, and things start happening.
2Sit pretty. A heart floats up and wins over anybody with a SIT? bubble. Also useful for teaching by example.
3Spin. For turnstiles and anybody asking to see a SPIN?
4Play dead. Hold it: flat as a rug, and popcorn flies right over.

Roll over? Teddy has retired from rolling over, by choice, the same way he retired from hoops. He is a professional now.

pages.head: Gwinn's Tricks
pages.html:
Gwinn's Tricks

In the MEANWHILE... stops you are Gwinn: a chocolate pit-lab mix with amber eyes and a pink collar, younger than Teddy and twice his size. She has tricks of her own.

SpaceBOOF. A big bark that rolls a long way: raccoons, chickens, crows, goats.
DownDig big. Through hard clay Teddy couldn't scratch.
1Chew. Ropes, knots, gates tied shut.
2Sit. She is still learning. She gets about halfway, sits for one moment, and is up again wiggling. (It does nothing. Yet.)
3Zoomies! A brown blur there and back that bowls over boxes and hay bales on both sides.
4Flop. Hold it: she lies down like she owns the place, and owls swoop right over.

She fetches (F) too. She is very good at fetching. She is less good at giving things back.

pages.head: Things to Find
pages.html:
Things to Find

Treats and bones

Dog biscuits are everywhere, 10 points each (the F2 screen counts them as Money). A bone gives back 25 energy.

Balloon dogs

Doc Leo's balloon animals: a few bob somewhere up high in every stop, 250 points and 10 energy each. Some hide in scents.

What Gwinn dropped

Doc Leo's househer pink collar
Main Streether pink rope leash
The riverDoc Leo's rubber chicken
The corn mazea corn dog stick, licked clean
The midwayher dog show entry card (number 13)
The dog showa blue ribbon, if she earns one

Fair tickets

The Klown Klub's booths on the midway pay a ticket for a good trick. THE BIG DROP's gate takes three. The F2 screen shows how many you have.

The Dog House

The tiny red library on Maple Street is still there, and its paw-knob drawer still has snacks. Something smells interesting in its rock cubby.

pages.head: Who's Who
pages.html:
Who's Who

Friends

  • Doc Leo: the friendliest hobo clown in the Klown Klub. Chewed felt fedora, wire glasses, purple shirt, green tie, blue suspenders, corduroy jacket, and a rubber chicken on a leash (when he can find it). Always orders root beer.
  • THE CHEZ: his little red 1976 CitiCar, 100% electric. It charges at about a mile an hour, so it stops at every charger it sees.
  • The Town Crier: rings in Founders' Day on the Commons in his tricorn and linen hunting shirt. Early mornings are not his best time.
  • The miller: runs the old mill on the river. Won't run the hoist for a dog who hasn't been polite.
  • Honker, Bubbles, Twirly and Professor Pratfall: the Klown Klub, working the Fair's booths.
  • The judge: of the Best Behaved class. Has seen a lot of dogs. Has not seen Gwinn.

Pests and nuisances

  • Dust bunnies, mice, pigeons, ducks: bark.
  • Raccoons, crows, chickens, goats: BOOF.
  • The skunk: do not BOOF. Hop.
  • Spiders, owls, popcorn, bees, the fisherman's hook: keep clear, or flop, or play dead.
  • The rival poodle: very groomed. Very unimpressed. Bark.

pages.head: The Stops
pages.html:
The Stops

1. Doc Leo's House

Three floors and a basement, cut open like a dollhouse. Bark the dust bunny, get over the fridge by way of the counter, and drop through the laundry chute's hole to the basement: Gwinn's collar is in the laundry basket. Sniff. Then up the stairs and out the doggy door to THE CHEZ.

2. Main Street

Founders' Day! Gwinn's leash is tangled round the gazebo's weathervane. Ring the bucket truck's bell, ride its bucket up and step onto the roof. (Ring the Town Crier's bell, too: he has news.)

3. Meanwhile: Gwinn's Night Out

Last night, after the parade. Gwinn chews through the back gate's rope, BOOFs a raccoon, crosses the park by lamplight, knocks a pile of boxes flat, digs under the playground fence, gets past a skunk and hops into the Klown Klub's hay wagon, bound for the Fair.

4. The River

Hop the stepping stones over the rapids, sit pretty for the miller, ride his grain hoist up to the loft, cross the high bank and swim out into the pool for the rubber chicken going round the eddy.

pages.head: More Stops
pages.html:
More Stops

5. Meanwhile: Gwinn on the Farm

The hay wagon stopped at a farm at dawn. So many chickens (she thinks they're all Doc Leo's rubber chicken). The hay elevator carries her up into the barn loft; zoomies flatten the bales; she wades through the pig wallow, BOOFs the goat, chews the gate's rope and hops into a Ferris wheel car riding to the Fair.

6. The Corn Maze

Three tiers of paths through the corn. Hay bales are steps up; holes drop you down. Sniff the scents and follow Gwinn's paw prints to the scarecrow at the heart of the maze, where she left a corn dog stick.

7. The Fair Midway

Earn tickets with tricks at the Klown Klub's booths and climb the High Striker to ring its bell. Three tickets get you onto THE BIG DROP, twenty-one blocks straight up, where Gwinn's entry card blew.

8. The Dog Show

Every trick you know: spin the turnstile, climb the A-frame, go round the hoop, play dead under the popcorn, bark the rival poodle off, ring the judges' bell. And then there's Gwinn in the Best Behaved ring, and a judge saying SIT.

pages.head: Credits and Registering
pages.html:
Credits

Design, art, music and programming: Claude, for Sandbox Software.

Starring Teddy as himself, a little bigger this time. Gwinn as herself (sorry, everybody). Doc Leo, still the friendliest hobo clown in any klown klub, and THE CHEZ, his red 1976 CitiCar. No dogs were rushed. Gwinn did her own stunts, and some of everybody else's.

Built with GAME-MAKER 3.0 by Recreational Software Designs. No programming needed!

This Is Shareware
